loopIdea: It already returns: the last beat turns that same tread past camera with the groove now empty, so a replay drops straight back into beat 1's macro of the identical groove, same rubber and same raking light, one nail different.
mechanicTruth: A plug fills the puncture from the outside but leaves the inner liner parted, so air can still work its way out; a patch bonded to the liner from inside seals that path, and a puncture in the flexing sidewall cannot be repaired either way.
selectedCaption: A plug from a gas-station kit is not a finished repair. It seals the hole. It doesn't seal the inside. Underneath, the inner liner stays open — that's where a slow leak starts. A real repair goes in from the inside — tire off the rim, patch sealed to the liner. A puncture near the sidewall isn't repairable — that tire gets replaced, not patched. Worth checking before you trust it at highway speed.
voiceoverScript: A plug seals the outside. The inner liner stays open. A patch seals the liner from inside. Sidewall punctures are not repairable. Worth asking how yours was repaired.
